title: The naive framing: "fifty separate conversations"
text: You might picture 50 separate chats, each with an analyst running together. That's not it. One call and the server spawns 50 sessions for you. So, how does one agent coordinate dozens without blocking?

title: The question: coordinate dozens without blocking
text: The question, how does a single agent coordinate long-running parallel sub-agents without opening multiple separate conversations or blocking the whole flow? The natural guess, to get three analysts

title: The wrong guess: three chats, copied by hand
text: Working at once, you open three separate Claude conversations yourself and copy the results between them by hand. A custom tool becomes the orchestration

title: The mechanism: a custom tool the server intercepts
text: Trigger. When the head agent calls dispatch analysts with a list of tickers, the server intercepts that call. It doesn't run the analysis itself. It spawns three independent analyst sessions, each with its own full context window, each running in parallel. The head agent pauses. The server monitors the sessions. title: The anchor: NVDA, AMD, MU — one flow
text: Research receives the prompt, sweep NVDA, AMD, and MU ranked by margin durability. It calls dispatch analysts with the three tickers. The server intercepts. Three analyst sessions spawn simultaneously. Each reads 20 pages of SEC filings independently, scores on a rubric, returns a grade. The head waits. It doesn't block your terminal. It doesn't lock the conversation. The server monitors all three in the background. When all three finish, NVDA scores nine, AMD scores six, MU scores four. The head resumes, reads the accumulated table, synthesizes a ranked report. One conversation, three parallel analysts, one merged report. The spread

title: The mechanism: isolated sessions, server as coordinator
text: Is the mechanism. One call fans out into N parallel sessions. Each session is fully isolated, its own context, its own tools, its own errors. They converge when they finish, not when the head decides to check. The server is the coordinator, not the agent. The timing

title: The anchor returns: fifty analysts, 25 minutes to 30 seconds
text: Difference is not incremental. It is categorical. Serial execution, 50 analysts, each taking 30 seconds one after another. That is 25 minutes. title: Fan-in: the aggregator deduplicates, ranks, merges
text: Results don't merge themselves. Each session returns its result as a chip, ticker, score, findings. The chips arrive at different times. The aggregator holds them until the last one lands, then runs three operations to duplicate, rank by score, merge into one structured report. It is not smart, it is a collector that waits for the full set before it hands anything back. Both

title: Both directions: the schema contract, kept and skipped
text: Sides follow a fixed contract. The head sends a task ID, ticker, and query focus. The analyst returns a task ID, findings, confidence, and sources. The aggregator checks every result against that shape. An off-schema result gets rejected on its own. One broken session doesn't corrupt the others. Skip the contract and one bad session can corrupt the merged report silently instead.
